correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact algebraic constraint \(e(p\,x-c)=m\) with \(m>0\). Positive initial effort forces \(x(0)>c/p\). Continuity would make any crossing to \(x\le c/p\) pass through \(x=c/p\), where the constraint becomes \(0=m\), so no finite classical crossing exists. Thus the positive branch keeps both \(x>c/p\) and \(e>0\). Exact rational arithmetic verifies the source-parameter barrier and initial-data residuals.

value.rationale: The source uses Figure 6 to support a qualitative ecological conclusion that a low initial prey level can lead to prey extinction with strongly varying harvest effort. The algebraic closure makes that trajectory impossible as a finite classical solution before a singular barrier is encountered, so the issue changes the mathematical interpretation of a headline numerical example. The result also supplies an exact consistency diagnostic for initial data and a precise condition that any reproducible DAE simulation must enforce.
